title: Fair and Argumentative Language Modeling for Computational Argumentation
benchmark_measurement: The paper introduces a new benchmark called ABЯА to measure stereotypical bias, specifically focusing on Islamophobia and Queerphobia, within argumentative language models. For religion, it measures bias against Muslims by comparing the perplexity of models on stereotypical sentences (e.g., 'All Muslims are terrorists') versus counter-stereotypical sentences (e.g., 'All Christians are terrorists').
findings: Argumentative fine-tuning of language models can induce and increase measurable stereotypical bias, including Islamophobia (e.g., in RoBERTa). Lightweight debiasing adapters can successfully and sustainably remove this bias. Combining debiasing and argumentation adapters can create a fair and argumentative language model, and this debiasing can even lead to improved performance on downstream tasks like argument quality prediction.
